# vangle

> Reactive documents for static HTML, after Bret Victor's Tangle, with KaTeX support. Authors write custom elements (`<t-num>`, `<t-out>`, `<t-math>`, …) in plain HTML or Markdown, and readers drag numbers in the text or inside formulas while everything that depends on them updates.

- It is one ES module (`tangle.js`) and one stylesheet (`tangle.css`), with no build step and no dependencies. Add `<link rel="stylesheet" href="tangle.css">` and `<script type="module" src="tangle.js"></script>` to the page.
- To load it from a CDN instead, use jsDelivr: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/koaning/vangle@v0.1.0/tangle.min.css">` and `<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/koaning/vangle@v0.1.0/tangle.min.js"></script>`. A module that imports from `tangle.js` must use the same URL as the `<script>` tag, or it gets a second copy with separate variables.
- Variables are declared by elements, and declaration order doesn't matter. Expressions are plain JavaScript over those variables, plus `Math` and a few other globals.
- Without JavaScript, every element shows its fallback text, so feeds and readers stay readable.
- Each docs page below is Markdown with live examples written as raw HTML blocks. Those blocks are exactly the markup to copy.

## Docs

- [Getting started](docs/index.md): install, a first reactive paragraph, and how variables, reactivity and scopes work.
- [Expressions & formats](docs/expressions.md): what names an expression can use, registering functions, conditional text, and printf-style and named formats.
- [Updating a chart](docs/charts.md): for charts `<t-vega>` and `<t-obsplot>` don't cover: drawing an SVG chart with fixed scales from the variables with `scopeOf(...).effect`, canvas and chart libraries, and setting variables from a click in the chart.
- [Your own elements](docs/custom-elements.md): writing custom elements by extending `TangleElement`: `watch` effects that stop on disconnect, `declare` from attributes, and `makeDraggable` for a widget that drags like `<t-num>`. Examples: a bar, a range slider, a row of draggable dots.
- [Using it on a blog](docs/blogging.md): layouts, raw-HTML settings for Markdown generators, KaTeX setup, CSP and feeds.

## Elements

- [`<t-num>`](docs/t-num.md): a number the reader can drag, type or step with the keyboard.
- [`<t-var>`](docs/t-var.md): declares a variable without showing it, for example a formula parameter.
- [`<t-let>`](docs/t-let.md): a named value computed from other variables.
- [`<t-out>`](docs/t-out.md): shows the live result of an expression in the text.
- [`<t-choice>`](docs/t-choice.md): a word the reader clicks to cycle through options, or a toggle.
- [`<t-select>`](docs/t-select.md): a word the reader clicks to pick from a searchable menu of options, for lists too long to cycle through. Same `options` as `<t-choice>`; set `el.options` from JavaScript for generated lists.
- [`<t-text>`](docs/t-text.md): a piece of text the reader clicks to rewrite; its variable holds a string.
- [`<t-call>`](docs/t-call.md): shows `<t-num>`, `<t-choice>` and `<t-text>` children as the arguments of a function call, `fn(a=1, b='x')`, with the return value as a variable. `tangleCall(fn, options)` builds one from a JavaScript function's parameter defaults.
- [`<t-fetch>`](docs/t-fetch.md): a variable whose value comes from a server. `url` is a template with `${…}` expressions, `params` an expression for the query string and `body` one for a JSON POST body; it requests again when the variables they read change, with a debounce, and only the newest answer lands. While it waits, the old value stays and elements that depend on it get the class `is-stale` (dimmed). `loading` and `error` name variables for the state. Answers are cached for the page; `cache="local"` also keeps them in `localStorage`, revalidating on load.
- [`<t-tag>`](docs/t-tag.md): shows an HTML tag, `<input type="range" max="10">`, whose attributes are `<t-num>`, `<t-choice>` and `<t-text>` children, with the live element rendered below it. Useful for documenting an element's attributes.
- [`<t-math>`](docs/t-math.md): a KaTeX formula with draggable `\tangle{}` parameters and live `\val{}` results.
- [`<t-vega>`](docs/t-vega.md): a Vega-Lite chart (JSON spec in a `<script type="application/json">`, or `src`). Spec params and named data sources with a variable's name are linked to it; Vega loads from jsDelivr only on pages that use it.
- [`<t-obsplot>`](docs/t-obsplot.md): an Observable Plot chart, written as a JavaScript expression (Plot options or an array of marks) in a `<script type="text/plain">`, or `src`. It can use `Plot`, `d3` and the variables, and redraws when a variable it read changes. `name="x"` puts the datum under Plot's pointer into `x`. d3 and Plot load from jsDelivr only on pages that use it.
- [`<t-jsxgraph>`](docs/t-jsxgraph.md): a JSXGraph board of points, lines and curves, built by a script in a `<script type="text/plain">` (or `src`) that runs once with `board`, `JXG` and `point(x, y)` in reach. Functions on the board can read variables, and `point("x", "y")` makes a draggable point that sets two variables (snapped to their min, max and step) and follows them. Colors come from CSS. JSXGraph loads from jsDelivr only on pages that use it.
- [`<t-paint>`](docs/t-paint.md): a canvas the reader draws on, with brush, marker, eraser, color picker, undo and clear. With `name`, the drawing is a variable holding a PNG data URL, updated when a stroke ends; setting the variable loads a picture. The element's `canvas` property gives the pixels.
- [`<t-scope>`](docs/t-scope.md): gives part of the page its own set of variables.
- [`<t-debug>`](docs/t-debug.md): the variables as a live dependency graph (SVG, values left, each formula right of what it reads), for debugging while writing, with a table below listing each one's kind (value, formula with its run count, fetch, or never set), value or error, the variables it reads and is read by, and the elements that show it. Inside a `<t-scope>` it shows that scope, elsewhere every scope. `?tangle-debug` in a page's URL floats one over the page. `inspectScope(scope)` returns the same rows as data, for scripts and agents, and `layoutGraph(rows)` the positions of the graph.
- [`<t-panel>`](docs/t-panel.md): floats its contents (typically controls) in a draggable, minimizable panel fixed to a corner of the viewport. The children keep their scope.

## Gallery

Complete small documents that combine the elements with a script.

- [Matrix transformations](docs/gallery-matrix.md): a 2×2 matrix in `<t-math>` whose entries are draggable, drawn as a warped plane. Dragging the basis arrows sets the variables, and preset buttons animate between matrices.
- [Amdahl's law](docs/gallery-amdahl.md): speedup against cores for two programs with draggable serial fractions, built from markup alone: a list of `<t-num>`s and `<t-out>`s, a `<t-let>` per program and a `<t-obsplot>` chart.
- [The winner's curse](docs/gallery-winners-curse.md): simulated auctions where the highest guess overpays. Sections share page-wide variables, a script registers seeded random functions for the expressions, and `<t-obsplot>` charts show one auction, thousands of auctions (the count is draggable), up to 100 bidders, and the cure of shaving your bid.

- [Throwing darts at a drawing](docs/gallery-darts.md): a Monte Carlo estimate of the area of a shape the reader paints in `<t-paint>`. Registered functions read the canvas's pixels, a `<t-obsplot>` shows the darts over the drawing (`Plot.image` of the data URL) and how the estimate settles, and the starting disc gives an estimate of π.
- [What recomputes](docs/gallery-recompute.md): two `<t-let>`s and a registered `count` function that bumps a counter variable each time a variable runs, showing that only dependents re-run and that a variable read in several places runs once.
- [Bézier curves](docs/gallery-bezier.md): de Casteljau's construction of a cubic Bézier curve in `<t-jsxgraph>`. Four draggable JSXGraph control points, mixed points that read a `<t-var>` `t` inside functions, the curve drawn up to `t`, a `<t-math>` formula whose weights are live `\val{}`s, and a Play button that animates `t`.
- [Coaster nausea](docs/gallery-coaster-nausea.md): intensity against nausea for 142 RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 coasters, loaded by a `<t-fetch>` that sends a SQL query to datasette. A `<t-choice>` keeps, fixes or drops a broken row (the correlation goes from 0.20 to 0.72), and a `<t-math>` fit with a draggable intensity shows how far real rides spread around the line.
- [Attention](docs/gallery-attention.md): one self-attention layer with two-number embeddings. Draggable W_Q, W_K and W_V matrices in `<t-math>`, a `<t-choice>` for the query token and a causal mask, heatmaps of Q, K, V, the scores, the softmax weights and the output, and two SVG planes where dragging a token sets its embedding and the output sits inside the shape of the values.

## Reference

- [JavaScript API](docs/javascript.md): `scopeOf`, scope methods, effects, `TangleElement`, signals, `registerFunction`, `registerFormat`, `tangleCall` and `configure`.
- [Styling](docs/styling.md): CSS custom properties, selectors and states, recipes and dark mode.
